name: Thieves' Vinegar
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: large handful of lavender blossoms
ingredients.originalText: a large handful of lavender blossoms

ingredients.name: strong clear vinegar
ingredients.originalText: three quarts of strong clear vinegar

instructions.text: Chop and mix lavender blossoms, sage, mint, rue, wormwood and rosemary well
Put them into a jar, with half an ounce of camphor that has been dissolved in a little alcohol
Pour in three quarts of strong clear vinegar
Keep the jar for two or three weeks in the hot sun, and at night plunge it into a box of heated sand
Strain and bottle the liquid, putting into each bottle a clove of garlic sliced
After it has been bottled for a week, pour it off carefully from the sediment and filter it through blotting paper
Wash the bottles and return the vinegar to them

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Chop and mix lavender blossoms, sage, mint, rue, wormwood and rosemary well
2. Put them into a jar, with half an ounce of camphor that has been dissolved in a little alcohol
3. Pour in three quarts of strong clear vinegar
4. Keep the jar for two or three weeks in the hot sun, and at night plunge it into a box of heated sand
5. Strain and bottle the liquid, putting into each bottle a clove of garlic sliced
6. After it has been bottled for a week, pour it off carefully from the sediment and filter it through blotting paper
7. Wash the bottles and return the vinegar to them
8. Keep it very tightly corked
